- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > 0.0) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the decline; increase forecast slope downward to match sentiment-driven bearish momentum.  
- Model frequently underestimates short-term mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 7-day average is > 10% above 30-day average, adjust forecast to align with 7-day mean reversion.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., negative → positive → negative), model tends to lag in recognizing turning points; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to capture sentiment-driven reversal.
